newsitem.title: FRANCE: France selling 24.9 mln Elf shares.
newsitem.headline: France selling 24.9 mln Elf shares.

text.p: The French finance ministry said on Wednesday it was selling 24.9 million shares in Elf-Aquitaine held through the ERAP holding company for about 10 billion francs.
An Elf spokesman said the Elf group, through its Fingestval company, bought 4.5 percent of the capital being sold by the government.
The ministry said in a statement the disposal will reduce its stake in Elf to 0.75 percent of the capital, this residual amount representing the free shares reserved for Elf employees.
The sale received prior approval of the Erap board, it said.
Some 12,584,240 shares, or 4.6 percent of the capital, were sold after a tender with various banks and placed in the market through Paribas and SBC Warburg.
Fingestval, indirectly owned by the Elf group, bought 12,315,760 shares, representing 4.5 percent of the stock.
The 10 billion franc sale proceeds will go into a special account for revenues from sales of shares in public sector companies to be used for injecting into state owned firms, it said.
ABN Amro was adviser bank to the government on the sale.
